doc.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

chapter: Church, energy and the state of jazz
title: Working with the musicians' union to cover jazz and rock players
summary: Cranshaw is a liaison between the union and jazz and rock musicians, as with the Lincoln Center Orchestra, to get pension and welfare benefits through dialogue.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well I mean I’m moving, but I understand, because of the business. So now, talking to younger players, right now I’m working with the union now to get into something else. Because they’re not involved in Broadway shows, because they’re not involved with the symphonies and the things that are already plugged into the musician’s union. I’m trying to see if I can help the union find ways to plug the jazz musicians and the rock musicians into the mainstream so that we don’t have to do benefits for a guy when he passes or this kind of thing, but to be able to have the pension and welfare that I’m a part of through the Broadway shows and the T.V. shows, and without even thinking about it. I was saying I used to go in the pit and all the guys would be sitting and they would be talking about the pension and I’m trying to figure out now why are they talking about pensions and stuff, and they’re not interested in playing music. I wanted to go and burn. I was ready to cook. I mean I was just thinking about the music. I didn’t care whether there was any pension or welfare. I should have been thinking about it. But because I was not plugged in to that situation, I didn’t think about it. Now I understand. So I have to make my colleagues from back there and the newer musicians aware that these things are there for them. But I’m trying to get, we have the Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis, we already got their group involved with the union so that they have things coming. If you’re going to belong to the union, the union should be able to do something for you. You should have something coming from it. If not, then I tell a young musician don’t join the union. But I say the same thing to the union. Rather than to argue with the union or be
angry at the union for what they don’t do, I’m a part of the union. So when they talk about the union they’re also talking about me. I’m the part that they’re talking about.

So rather than to get out of it, I got into it. I said okay, I’m not going to fight the union, I have to help the union, but I have to be a liaison between what the union would like to do and what the guys would like to do. And it’s easier for me to go and talk to the jazz musicians or the rock musicians ‘cause they know me, about a situation, and not do anything unless they want me to do it, rather than having a union representative come in and say, you know, you guys have to do that. I don’t like that. My back goes up if they do it to me. So I’m starting to get dialogue going for, we have it for Lincoln Center and we’re trying to do it for the Carnegie Hall Orchestra without disturbing what they already have going. Because we have to take into consideration that the George Weins and the people that are supplying so many weeks of work for these people, so it’s a working — it’s got to be a working thing where it works for the employer and it works for the musicians. But we never had dialogue going between the two vested situations. The union was always going in and saying well you’ve got to do this, and of course when you tell somebody they’ve got to do it their back goes up so you start to fight it. Let’s talk and see what we have coming, how it’s going to benefit the guys before we even think about doing anything. And this is what I’m about. I want to make sure that everybody is going to be covered. Other than that, don’t bother me. I don’t have anything invested and you can’t make my situation work for me through the union then I shouldn’t be there, I should be somewhere else where they work for me. And this is what I’m about as a business.
